title: Automated Infrastructure Provisioning for Edge Applications
business: A distributed software consultancy managing hundreds of micro-services for global retail clients.
problem: Manual configuration of edge storage and database resources across multiple Cloudflare accounts creates significant operational overhead and leads to inconsistent environment setups.
solution: By utilizing the Cloudflare Developer Platform connector within Claude, engineers can programmatically manage infrastructure primitives like D1 databases and R2 buckets directly through natural language prompts, ensuring standardized environment creation.
steps: Authenticate the Cloudflare MCP connector within the Claude interface to establish secure access to your Cloudflare account.
Use the connector to list existing D1 databases and R2 buckets to verify current environment state.
Issue a prompt to create new D1 database instances and R2 buckets for a specific client project.
Verify the successful creation of resources by querying the updated list of namespaces and databases via the connector tools.
outcome: The consultancy achieves rapid, consistent environment parity across all client projects, reducing the time spent on manual infrastructure provisioning tasks.
limitation: The connector operates based on the permissions of the authenticated account; if the account lacks specific API scopes, resource creation will fail. Users must verify the active account context using set_active_account before executing provisioning commands.
